Startup ships neuromorphic edge chips for battery sensors

A startup has begun shipping neuromorphic edge chips to industrial customers, the first commercial deliveries after two years of pilots. The spiking processors run keyword spotting and anomaly detection on coin-cell batteries.

The company says its neuromorphic edge chips plug into standard EDA flows, which lets microcontroller vendors license the core instead of building their own accelerators. Early customers include two factory-automation vendors.
